messages:
Anika: Hey all — pulling together a 6-12mo plan for routing + multi-region tenant isolation. Need alignment on launch criteria, customer-driven asks, and which approach to prioritize (soft isolation vs dedicated slices).
Raj: Posted an initial sketch in the RFC channel: https://redwood.internal/rfc/tenant-bubbles (rough)
Jia: Top compliance asks so far: per-tenant VPC peering, egress controls, and immutable audit trails for model inputs.
Devon: Also from large AI-native customers: deterministic low-latency lanes. They prefer dedicated infra for tail latency.
Ben: Quick framing q: do we aim for 'tenant bubbles' (logical isolation + runtime policies) or hard slices (reserved GPUs, separate pools)? different ops story.
Laura: From an SRE stance: bubbles are faster to roll out and cheaper, hard slices give stronger SLA and isolation guarantees.
Anika: @Devon can you surface perf deltas and cost delta between bubble vs hard-slice by EOD Fri? we need numbers to justify prioritization.
Devon: Short numbers from perf run this week: bubble -> p50 ~95ms, p99 ~420ms; hard-slice -> p50 ~65ms, p99 ~120ms. Estimated infra cost +~40% for hard slices at current utilization.
Raj: Proposed launch gates (draft): 1) Canary w/2 real tenants + synthetic stress 2) SLA gate: p99 < 250ms under peak 3) Isolation gate: KV/cache leakage tests pass 4) Failover gate: automated fallback to compatible model variant works.
Jia: Add compliance gate: KMS integration verified + audit logs retained 90d and accessible to compliance team.
Ben: Ops/runbook items: eviction mechanics, soft eviction alerts, customer notification flows, and a consistent fallback policy to degrade gracefully (model variant or lower throughput tier).
Anika: Prioritization idea: pilot hard-slice for customers > $250k ARR or those with explicit latency SLAs; expose bubbles as opt-in cheaper path for devs.
ops-bot: ops-bot: RFC tenant-bubbles-routing.md uploaded to /rfc/; reviewers requested: @Anika @Raj @Jia @Devon
Devon: I will run a detailed 99th-percentile sweep across sequence lengths and share a perf deck by next Wed.
Laura: Also need a migration path doc: how customers move between bubbles <-> hard-slice, and a cost modelling spreadsheet to show delta.
Anika: Action items recap: 1) Devon perf deck + tail tests 2) Raj formalize launch gates doc 3) Jia compliance checklist w/owners 4) Ben draft ops runbook + eviction playbook 5) Raj/Laura cost model. Sync next Tue 10:00am PT. :eyes:
Ben: +1. I'll start the runbook template and link to runbooks repo.
Jia: I'll reach out to security to lock down KMS acceptance criteria.
Raj: I'll convert the sketch into a decision matrix (latency-first vs cost-first) and throw it in the RFC this week.
Anika: Thanks — want a short executive summary for product leadership by end of week. Keep notes here, will assemble.
